content.explanation: JavaScript runs inside a sandbox, which is a restricted environment controlled by the browser. This prevents websites from directly reading files, executing operating system commands, or accessing hardware resources without permission. Sandboxing protects users from malicious websites and helps isolate websites from each other.
content.example: JavaScript cannot freely browse your hard drive and read personal documents.
content.analogy: A sandbox lets children play safely within boundaries.
content.keyTakeaway: Sandboxing protects users from untrusted code.
